facts.statement: The animal is classified under the genus Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: taxon: Argentinosaurus

facts.statement: The genus was described by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: authority: Bonaparte & Coria, 1993

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Argentinosaurus huinculensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Argentinosaurus huinculensis

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur meaning "lizard from Argentina".
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the animal measured 30 to 35 meters long and weighed 65 to 80 tonnes.
facts.quote: measuring 30 - 35 m long and weighing 65 - 80 t

facts.statement: The first bone was discovered in 1987 by a farmer near Plaza Huincul.
facts.quote: The first Argentinosaurus bone was discovered in 1987 by a farmer on his farm near the city of Plaza Huincul

facts.statement: A scientific excavation led by José Bonaparte took place in 1989.
facts.quote: A scientific excavation of the site led by the Argentine palaeontologist José Bonaparte was conducted in 1989

facts.statement: The first bone, now identified as a fibula, was discovered in 1987 by Guillermo Heredia.
facts.quote: The first Argentinosaurus bone, which is now thought to be a fibula (calf bone), was discovered in 1987 by Guillermo Heredia

facts.statement: The discovery site was located about 8 km east of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: about 8 km east of Plaza Huincul, in Neuquén Province, Argentina

facts.statement: The formal description was published in 1993 by Bonaparte and Rodolfo Coria.
facts.quote: The formal description was published in 1993 by Bonaparte and the Argentine palaeontologist Rodolfo Coria

facts.statement: The limb bone found in 1987 was originally described as a tibia but was reidentified as a left fibula in 2004 by Mazzetta and colleagues.
facts.quote: Bonaparte and Coria described the limb bone discovered in 1987 as an eroded tibia (shin bone), although the Uruguayan palaeontologist Gerardo Mazzetta and colleagues reidentified this bone as a left fibula in 2004

facts.statement: In 1996, Bonaparte assigned a complete femur from the same locality to the genus.
facts.quote: In 1996, Bonaparte referred (assigned) a complete femur (thigh bone) from the same locality to the genus

facts.statement: As of 2019, it remained uncertain whether the femora found belonged to Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: As of 2019, however, it was still uncertain whether any of these femora belonged to Argentinosaurus

facts.statement: Fossils were recovered from the Huincul Formation, deposited in the Albian stage.
facts.quote: The fossils of Argentinosaurus were recovered from the Huincul Formation, which was deposited in the Albian stage

facts.statement: The fragmentary nature of the remains makes interpreting the animal difficult.
facts.quote: The fragmentary nature of Argentinosaurus remains makes their interpretation difficult

facts.statement: There is disagreement over whether Argentinosaurus was the largest known titanosaur.
facts.quote: there is disagreement over whether it was the largest known titanosaur

facts.statement: In 2019, Paul found Patagotitan to be smaller than Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: However, Paul found Patagotitan to be smaller than Argentinosaurus in 2019

facts.statement: The animal was a member of Titanosauria, the dominant sauropod group during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous

facts.statement: A reconstructed dorsal vertebra of Argentinosaurus is 159 cm high and 129 cm wide.
facts.quote: one dorsal vertebra has a reconstructed height of 159 cm and a width of 129 cm

facts.statement: The centra of Argentinosaurus dorsal vertebrae can be up to 57 cm wide.
facts.quote: the vertebral centra are up to 57 cm in width

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Argentinosaurus were opisthocoelous, meaning they were concave at the rear.
facts.quote: The dorsals were opisthocoelous (concave at the rear) as in other macronarian sauropods

facts.statement: The dorsal ribs of Argentinosaurus were tubular and cylindrical, unlike those of other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The dorsal ribs were tubular and cylindrical in shape, in contrast with other titanosaurs

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus likely had six sacral vertebrae, similar to many other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus, like many titanosaurs, probably had six sacral vertebrae

facts.statement: The complete femur assigned to Argentinosaurus is 2.5 meters long.
facts.quote: The complete femur that was assigned to Argentinosaurus is 2.5 m long

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues estimated the original length of the Argentinosaurus femur at 2.557 meters.
facts.quote: Mazzetta and colleagues used regression equations to estimate its original length at 2.557 m

facts.statement: In 2019, Paul estimated the original length of the Argentinosaurus femur at 2.575 meters.
facts.quote: later in 2019 Paul gave a similar estimate of 2.575 m

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserves a slender bone 1.55 meters long, originally thought to be a tibia but now identified as a fibula.
facts.quote: it preserves a slender fibula (originally interpreted as a tibia) that is 1.55 m in length

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Coria proposed the family Andesauridae for Argentinosaurus, Andesaurus, and Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: Bonaparte and Coria proposed a separate family for the three genera, the Andesauridae

facts.statement: A 2003 study by Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Upchurch declared both Titanosauridae and Andesauridae invalid.
facts.quote: A 2003 study by Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Upchurch found both Titanosauridae and Andesauridae to be invalid

facts.statement: A 2017 study by Carballido and colleagues classified Argentinosaurus as a member of Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: A 2017 study by Carballido and colleagues recovered Argentinosaurus as a member of Lognkosauria

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Hesham Sallam and colleagues found conflicting phylogenetic positions for Argentinosaurus, placing it either as a basal titanosaur or as a sister taxon to Epachthosaurus.
facts.quote: Another 2018 study by Hesham Sallam and colleagues found two different phylogenetic positions for Argentinosaurus

facts.statement: Some authors argue that the hollow dorsal ribs of Argentinosaurus may be due to post-mortem erosion rather than being naturally hollow.
facts.quote: later authors argued this hollowing could also have been due to erosion after the death of the individual

facts.statement: It is debated whether the structures interpreted as hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in Argentinosaurus are actually thickened vertebral laminae.
facts.quote: Other authors argued most titanosaur genera lacked hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and that the articular structures seen in Epachthosaurus and Argentinosaurus are thickened vertebral laminae (ridges)

facts.statement: A 2019 study by González Riga and colleagues placed Argentinosaurus in Lognkosauria, which they grouped with Rinconsauria in a new clade named Colossosauria.
facts.quote: Another 2019 study by González Riga and colleagues also found Argentinosaurus to belong to Lognkosauria; they found this group to form a larger clade with Rinconsauria within Titanosauria, which they named Colossosauria

facts.statement: Guillermo Heredia discovered the bone remains of Argentinosaurus near Plaza Huincul in Argentine Patagonia.
facts.quote: Sus vestigios óseos fueron descubiertos por Guillermo Heredia, en una estancia rural cerca de Plaza Huincul, en la Patagonia argentina.

facts.statement: Intermediate estimates suggest Argentinosaurus was 33 to 36 meters long and weighed 70 to 80 tonnes.
facts.quote: De entre las diferentes estimaciones propuestas, un margen intermedio y probable estima a Argentinosaurus con 33-36 m de longitud y una masa corporal de 70-80 toneladas

facts.statement: Various studies have estimated Argentinosaurus to be between 30 and 39.7 meters long and weigh between 55 and 90 tonnes.
facts.quote: Diferentes estudios, a lo largo de los años, han estimado su tamaño en un rango de entre 30 a 39,7 m de longitud, con un peso de 55 a 90 tn

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus could reach a height of more than 16 meters when its neck was raised.
facts.quote: y una altura de más de 16 metros al erguir el cuello

facts.statement: In 2016, Mark Hallett and Matthew Wedel estimated that Argentinosaurus eggs were likely only 1 liter in volume.
facts.quote: In 2016, Mark Hallett and Matthew Wedel stated that the eggs of Argentinosaurus were probably only 1 L in volume

facts.statement: Hallett and Wedel estimated that a newly hatched Argentinosaurus was no longer than 1 meter and did not weigh more than 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: and that a hatched Argentinosaurus was no longer than 1 m and not heavier than 5 kg

facts.statement: It is suggested that Argentinosaurus may have been preyed upon by Mapusaurus, one of the largest known theropods.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus might have been preyed on by Mapusaurus, which is among the largest theropods known

facts.statement: Earlier research suggested the age of the deposits containing Argentinosaurus ranged from the Cenomanian–Turonian to the Early Turonian–Late Santonian.
facts.quote: Earlier findings suggested a Cenomanian–Turonian age, or possibly an Early Turonian to Late Santonian age

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation, where Argentinosaurus fossils were found, consists of fine-to-medium grain yellowish and greenish sandstones, some containing volcanic ash.
facts.quote: The Huincul Formation is composed of yellowish and greenish sandstones of fine-to-medium grain, some of which are tuffaceous

facts.statement: Fossilized pollen from the Huincul Formation indicates a diverse plant environment included hornworts, ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms.
facts.quote: Fossilised pollen indicates a wide variety of plants were present in the Huincul Formation

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation contains fossils of other sauropods, including the titanosaur Choconsaurus and rebbachisaurids like Cathartesaura and Limaysaurus.
facts.quote: In addition to Argentinosaurus, the sauropods of the Huincul Formation are represented by another titanosaur, Choconsaurus, and several rebbachisaurids including Cathartesaura, Limaysaurus, and some unnamed species

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation has yielded theropod fossils including Mapusaurus, Skorpiovenator, Huinculsaurus, Overoraptor, Aoniraptor, and Gualicho.
facts.quote: Theropods including carcharodontosaurids such as Mapusaurus, abelisaurids including Skorpiovenator, Ilokelesia, and Tralkasaurus, noasaurids such as Huinculsaurus, paravians such as Overoraptor, and other theropods such as Aoniraptor and Gualicho have also been discovered there

facts.statement: The genus Argentinosaurus was named by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte & Coria, 1993

facts.statement: The species A. huinculensis was named by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993.
facts.quote: species_authority: Bonaparte & Coria, 1993

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is classified within the family Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: familia: Lognkosauria

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus likely had a small head relative to its body, equipped with simple, long, thin, tubular teeth.
facts.quote: Argentinosaurus debió tener una cabeza bastante pequeña en proporción a su cuerpo, provista de simples pero largas coronas dentarias, delgadas y en forma de tubo

facts.statement: Sauropods, including Argentinosaurus, were oviparous, meaning they laid eggs.
facts.quote: Sauropods were oviparous (egg-laying)

facts.statement: Very little of Argentinosaurus has been recovered, including only some vertebrae, a fibula, fragmentary ribs, and the sacrum.
facts.quote: No se ha recuperado mucho de Argentinosaurus, apenas algunas vértebras, un peroné, costillas fragmentarias y el sacro.

facts.statement: Six dorsal vertebrae were described in detail, with the largest reaching 1.59 meters in height and 1.29 meters in width.
facts.quote: Seis vértebras dorsales fueran descritas detalladamente, la mayor de ellas alcanzando un tamaño de 1,59 m de alto con 1,29 m de ancho.

facts.statement: An incomplete femur, cataloged as MLP-DP 46-VIII-21-3, found near the excavation site is attributed to the same specimen.
facts.quote: Un fémur incompleto, MLP-DP 46-VIII-21-3, hallado no lejos de la zona de la excavación, se atribuye al mismo espécimen.

facts.statement: The original authors estimated the femur's total length was no less than 240 cm.
facts.quote: Según los autores originales su tamaño no debió ser menor a los 240 cm.

facts.statement: In 1996, paleontologist José Bonaparte estimated the femur length at 250 cm.
facts.quote: Posteriormente en 1996, fue el paleontólogo José Bonaparte quien estimó al fémur en 250 cm de largo.

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues estimated the femur length at 255.7 cm.
facts.quote: Similar al tamaño calculado por Mazzetta et al., quienes lo estimaron en 255,7 cm de longitud.

facts.statement: An early reconstruction by Gregory S. Paul estimated Argentinosaurus at 30 to 35 meters long and weighing 80 to 100 tons.
facts.quote: Una temprana reconstrucción de Gregory S. Paul estimó que Argentinosaurus midió entre 30 y 35 metros de longitud y que pesó de 80 a 100 toneladas.

facts.statement: A publication in Current Science later suggested a maximum estimate of 45 meters in length and 100 tons in weight.
facts.quote: Unos años más tarde, en una publicación de la revista Current Science, se le apunta con un estimado, máximo y liberal, de 45 metros y 100 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: In 2006, Kenneth Carpenter estimated Argentinosaurus at 30 meters long based on the most complete Saltasaurus specimen.
facts.quote: En 2006 Kenneth Carpenter se basa en el más completo espécimen de Saltasaurus como una guía para estimar a Argentinosaurus en 30 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Mazzetta and colleagues used femur regression equations to estimate an average weight of 73 tons, with a possible range of 60 to 88 tons.
facts.quote: Mazzetta y colaboradores utilizan ecuaciones de regresión, con datos extraídos de la anatomía del fémur (hueso clave en el soporte del peso del animal), y promedian un peso estimado de 73 toneladas, y ofrecen un amplio rango que va de 60 a 88 toneladas como su posible masa corporal.

facts.statement: In 2008, Jorge Calvo and colleagues estimated Argentinosaurus at 33 meters long.
facts.quote: En 2008, Jorge Calvo y colegas realizan una revisión de los tamaños estimados de titanosaurios, calculando a Argentinosaurus con 33 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus belongs to the parent group Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Argentinosaurus lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Because the only known specimen is very incompletely preserved, an exact estimate of its body dimensions cannot be confirmed until better-preserved specimens are found.
facts.quote: Debido al muy incompleto estado de preservación del único espécimen conocido, simplemente no es posible asegurar un estimado exacto de sus dimensiones corporales, hasta un futuro hallazgo de ejemplares mejor preservados.
